Thank you. We will now have today's invocation which will be delivered by Pastor Tiffany Triplett Henkel, the Executive Director of Metro Baptist Church, which is located at 410 West 14th Street in Manhattan. Welcome.

Divine Light and Weaver of justice. We give thanks for this day, for this session, and for the gift of serving and advocating for others. Remind us all of our kinship with one another, and with all of nature, so that we might live, work, govern, and engage in a spirit of abundance rather than scarcity, so that all may have enough and know that they are enough. I give thanks for these Council members and staff, and for the

NEW YORK CITY COUNCIL STATED MEETING 10 unique and important skills, and perspectives that they bring to this body, and thus to our city. Renew them in mind, body and spirit. Give them boldness to perform their duties with integrity. Grant them discernment when righteousness is ambiguous, and decisions are complex. Grant them courage when virtue is risky, and truth is unpopular. And finally, may they find joy, and fulfillment in uplifting the most vulnerable in our myths, remind each of us of the ways we hold power in systems. And let us engage that power to reverse the tide of oppression. We recognize in this great city that there is a great divide and disparity between the haves and the have nots. And remind us how much that that grieves you, and remind us that it does not have to be. Let us remember that none of us are whole unless all of us are whole. And let us get to the work of wholeness. And during this month of pride may we give thanks for the beautiful diversity of humanity and all creation. Let us rejoice that we live in a city that celebrates individuality and uniqueness of identity. Knowing that with each unique expression, we are granted a more holistic view of the Divine. And may we continue to work for

Thank you Majority Leader powers and thank you Reverend Henkel for that beautiful invocation. Reverend Tiffany Triplett Henkel is the pastor of Metro Baptist Church, and executive director of Rauschenbusch Metro Ministries in Hell's Kitchen, where she has been a resident and community leader for the past 17 years. At Metro Baptist, Reverend Henkel helps operate a renowned Food Pantry that's partially supplied by an incredible urban farm on the rooftop of the church. Her spouse is a small business owner in Hell's Kitchen and they're the parents of two children. In New York City Public Schools, Hudson River Middle School and Midtown West. I make a motion for unanimous consent to spread the invocation in full upon the record.
